question: What is a data mesh, what are Dehghani's four principles, and how should a practitioner judge whether a proposed solution is a real data mesh?
contributions: Explains Dehghani's four data mesh principles
Defines the 'pure' data mesh and why few real solutions qualify
Describes domain types, a logical architecture and three mesh topologies (Type 1-3)
Contrasts data mesh with data fabric and with data federation

limits: Serra states his skepticism openly ('I fall into the skeptics’ camp') and says 'this is all guesswork'.
The poll is anecdotal by his own account; no counts, venues or dates are given.
Gartner figures are quoted second-hand from the 2023 hype cycle and have dated.
Assessment of whether a mesh suits an organisation is deferred to Chapter 14, which is not in this PDF.
The PDF has no title page, author or year; chapter text refers to 'this book', Chapter 14 and Strengholt 2023.
practices: Treat data mesh as an organizational and cultural shift, not a technology (p.169).
Design domains and products carefully up front before building (pp.180-181).
Give domain teams a central self-serve platform so they do not rebuild infrastructure (p.175).
Automate governance policy implementation and monitoring and tag data (p.177).
Do not call data federation or per-department lakes a data mesh (pp.178, 183-184).
Use the Fig 13-4 centralisation spectrum to check whether a solution is mostly central (pp.184-185).

terms.definition: a decentralized data architecture with four specific characteristics
a self-contained, independently deployable unit of data that delivers business value
the idea that data owners treat data as a fully contained product they are responsible for, rather than a byproduct of a process that others manage
agreements between data domains or data products that define the format and structure of the data exchange between a producer and a consumer
analytical data that corresponds closely to the operational sources where the data originates
analytical data that combines and/or aggregates data from other domains, generally to help with query performance
analytical data that has been transformed to fit the needs of one or more specific departments or use cases
all domains use the same technology; one enterprise data lake with a container or folder per domain
same technology as Type 1 but each domain has its own data lake
each domain can use whatever technologies and cloud provider it wants
